stamp.heading: The mark
stamp.lead: The mark carries everything the inspector at the destination port needs. Here is each field on its own: what it means, and what happens when it is missing.

ippc.title: The IPPC symbol
ippc.what: The stylised wheat ear shows that the timber was treated under ISPM 15, the international plant protection standard.
ippc.without: Without it, customs at the destination treat the consignment as untreated timber.

lu.title: LU
lu.what: The ISO country code of the country where the timber was treated and marked.
lu.without: It tells the authority at the destination which register to check.

number.what: Our registration number with ASTA, the Administration des Services Techniques de l'Agriculture. It is unique, non-transferable and publicly verifiable.

code.title: The treatment code
code.what: It states how the timber was treated: HT for heat treatment, DB for debarked.
code.without: Without the code the mark is incomplete and therefore invalid.

twoSides.title: Two sides
twoSides.what: The mark must be applied visibly and permanently, preferably on two opposite sides.
twoSides.without: Then the inspector finds it no matter how the crate sits in the container.

noRedOrange.title: Not red, not orange
noRedOrange.what: Those colours are reserved for marking dangerous goods.
noRedOrange.without: Which is why you do not see them on this website either.

afterRepair.title: Marked again after every repair
afterRepair.what: If a pallet is reused, recycled or repaired, it has to be marked again, and every component has to be treated.
afterRepair.without: Which is why we do not only repair. We re-mark as well.

replaces.title: What it replaces
replaces.what: Inside the EU the mark replaces the plant passport; on export it replaces the phytosanitary certificate.
replaces.without: It applies to solid timber from 6 mm thick, not to processed wood panels.

history.heading: History

entries.1959: Henry Kasel founds a joinery with three employees in Bissen. Wooden packaging grows out of it step by step.
entries.1973: Maison Kasel is founded in Bissen.
entries.1994: 18 employees, capacity is exhausted. International customers want larger plant.
entries.1995: The move to the industrial estate in Mertzig, with storage and offices.
entries.1997: Two more storage halls. Total floor area has stood at 9,000 m² since then.
entries.2002: A thorough modernisation of every part of the works.
entries.2008: The new pallet machine goes into service.
entries.2014: Emballages en Bois Kasel S.à r.l. is founded under Tom Kasel and takes over production.

history.family: Pierrot Kasel succeeded his father Henry. The family still runs the administration. Tom Kasel heads the production company.

faq.heading: Frequently asked

china.q: Does my consignment to China need an IPPC mark?
china.a: Yes. China, Australia and New Zealand require ISPM 15 treated timber with a valid IPPC mark. We may apply it, registration number 079.

eu.a: No ISPM 15 treatment is required there. Where needed, the mark replaces the plant passport.

leadtime.a: We cut the timber once the order comes in, and we have 9,000 m² of storage. How long it takes in your case we will tell you as soon as we have read your request. Send us the quantity and the date you need it.

repair.q: Can you repair our used pallets?
repair.a: Yes, and we mark them again afterwards, as the standard requires.

storage.q: Can you store finished goods for us?
storage.a: Yes. Finished goods usually go straight out, but they can be stored and shipped on call-off.

sizes.a: Standard pallets, CP pallets and special pallets to your specification. Tell us the size you need. We cut to order and are not tied to stock sizes.

driver-access.a: Through the main hall. That is the only access to the yard and the ramp. The full route is on the Delivery & collection page.

crates.lead: Crates for sea freight of copper, glass, aluminium and machinery. Closed or slatted, according to weight and cargo.
crates.closedBody: Fully boarded. For glass and for anything that tolerates neither dust nor damp.
crates.slattedBody: Battens with gaps between them. Lighter and cheaper when the goods are stable in themselves. Typical for machinery and aluminium profiles.
crates.cargoBody: Copper, glass and aluminium go by sea most often. All three place different demands on the skids and on the securing. So send us the weight and the centre of gravity as well.
crates.exportBody: We hold the approval of the Service Technique de l'Agriculture for making pallets and crates that meet the import rules of China, Australia and New Zealand.

repair.lead: We repair used crates and pallets and put them back into service. Many of our packagings stay in use for several years that way.
repair.ruleBody: A pallet that is reused, recycled or repaired has to be marked again. Every component has to be treated. Only registered companies may do that. We are one, so you get the pallet back with a valid mark.

Replace broken boards, blocks and skids
Re-mark after repair, as the standard requires
Deliver back to your site or hold on call-off

ispm15.lead: ISPM 15 is the international standard for wood packaging in world trade. It exists to stop pests travelling from one continent to another inside packaging timber. Who may treat and mark under the standard is listed in a public register.
ispm15.whoHeading: Who may apply the mark in Luxembourg
ispm15.whoBody: Three companies. We are one of them, with registration number 079. The list is kept by ASTA and it is public.
rules: The mark must be permanent and must not be transferable.
It must be applied visibly, preferably on two opposite sides.
Red and orange are to be avoided, because those colours are reserved for dangerous goods.
If a pallet is reused, recycled or repaired, it must be marked again; every component must be treated.
The marking may only be destroyed by complete incineration.
It applies to solid timber from 6 mm thick, not to processed wood panels.
The mark replaces the plant passport in intra-EU movement and the phytosanitary certificate on export.
ispm15.whenBody: For China, Australia and New Zealand, always. For other third countries it depends on the destination. Put it in your request and we will tell you.

privacy.lead: In short: we set no cookies, we run no tracking, and the fonts and the map on this site do not load from anyone else's servers. Which is why there is no banner to click away.
privacy.whatBody: Only what you type into the request form yourself: company, contact person, email and the description of your job. Optionally phone, quantity, date needed, delivery location and, if you attach one, a file. If you use the configurator, the configured values travel with it. You see them on the page before you send.
privacy.whyBody: To answer your enquiry and, if it turns into an order, to carry it out.
privacy.legalBasisBody: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (steps prior to a contract) and, as far as the tick box is concerned, Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR (consent). You may withdraw consent at any time.
privacy.retentionBody: Requests that do not turn into an order are deleted after two years. Requests that do are kept as long as commercial and tax law requires. In Luxembourg, ten years.
privacy.processorsBody: The form runs through a server function at Supabase; processing takes place in the EU. The email itself goes through our mail provider. We do not pass your data on and we do not sell it.
privacy.hostingBody: The web server records technical access data, as every server does. Those logs are used only to run and secure the site.
privacy.cookiesBody: None. Neither ours nor anyone else's. There is no analytics either.
privacy.rightsBody: You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection. Write to {email} for that.
privacy.authorityBody: Commission nationale pour la protection des données (CNPD), 15, boulevard du Jazz, L-4370 Belvaux, Luxembourg.
